entities.name: Quintus Sulpicius Camerinus Praetextatus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Sulpicius Camerinus Praetextatus was a consul or consular tribune of the Roman Republic in 434 BC, marking a pivotal moment in the late Roman Republic's struggle for power.

As a key figure in this era, Camerinus played a role in shaping the fate of Rome through his political alliances and military campaigns.

His legacy can be seen in the subsequent power struggles that arose after his death, including the rise of Julius Caesar.

The oft-cited phrase ' Tempus fugit, meminisse nos' ('Time flees, let us remember') is attributed to Camerinus himself, highlighting the significance he placed on preserving Roman history and tradition.
